title: Analysing NanoDrop Spectra
text: parse_waves() pulls absorbance chosen wavelengths measurement compares pairs. type = "ratio" gives usual nucleic acid purity ratios: default type = "diff" gives differences, useful peak heights baseline: measurement row, identified measurement (file, data came read_nanodrop_dir()), even sample names repeat. average replicates, group whatever identifies sample. example file names like "6 1" "6 2" carry sample replicate number:

title: Analysing NanoDrop Spectra
text: output read_nanodrop() long table, dplyr summaries work directly:
code: spectra %>%   group_by(samps, measurement) %>%   summarise(     peak_wavelength = waves[which.max(abs)],     peak_abs = max(abs),     .groups = "drop"   ) %>%   head() #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   samps measurement peak_wavelength peak_abs #>   <chr>       <int>           <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 10 1           10            228.     23.8 #> 2 10 2           11            229      26.1 #> 3 11 1           12            230.     26.3 #> 4 11 2           13            228.     24.8 #> 5 12 1           14            230      26.4 #> 6 12 2           15            230.     26.1

title: Analysing NanoDrop Spectra
code: # Measurements with negative absorbance anywhere in the spectrum spectra %>%   filter(abs < 0) %>%   distinct(samps, measurement) #>      samps measurement #>     <char>       <int> #>  1:    7 1           3 #>  2:    9 1           7 #>  3:    9 2           8 #>  4:    9 3           9 #>  5:   10 1          10 #>  6:   11 2          13 #>  7:   13 2          17 #>  8:   15 1          20 #>  9:   15 2          21 #> 10:   15 3          22  # Every measurement should cover the same wavelengths spectra %>%   count(measurement) %>%   distinct(n) #>        n #>    <int> #> 1:  1321

title: Analysing NanoDrop Spectra
code: smoothed <- spectra %>%   filter(measurement <= 4) %>%   group_by(measurement) %>%   mutate(smoothed = predict(loess(abs ~ waves, span = 0.1))) %>%   ungroup()  ggplot(smoothed, aes(waves)) +   geom_line(aes(y = abs, colour = "Original")) +   geom_line(aes(y = smoothed, colour = "Smoothed")) +   facet_wrap(~samps) +   labs(x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = "Absorbance", colour = NULL) +   theme_minimal()

title: Analysing NanoDrop Spectra
code: ggplot(spectra, aes(waves, factor(measurement), fill = abs)) +   geom_raster() +   scale_fill_viridis_c() +   labs(x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = "Measurement", fill = "Absorbance") +   theme_minimal()

title: Importing NanoDrop Spectral Data
text: NanoDrop One UV-Vis export holds one block per measurement: sample name, timestamp, Wavelength (nm) header, // calibration lines, wavelength/absorbance pairs: read_nanodrop() turns long table one row per measurement wavelength.
code: 6 1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM Wavelength (nm) 10mm Absorbance //WLCalib: Shift    0.22333 ... //QSpecEnd: 190.0   10.666 190.5   10.782 ...

title: Importing NanoDrop Spectral Data
text: columns : samps: sample name typed instrument waves: wavelength (nm) abs: absorbance measurement: position block file. measure sample twice, two measurements stay separate. timestamp: timestamp line written instrument Use min_wv max_wv keep part spectrum:
code: library(nanodRop)  path <- system.file("extdata", "nanodrop_example.tsv", package = "nanodRop") spectra <- read_nanodrop(path) head(spectra) #>     samps waves    abs measurement         timestamp #>    <char> <num>  <num>       <int>            <char> #> 1:    6 1 190.0 10.666           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM #> 2:    6 1 190.5 10.782           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM #> 3:    6 1 191.0 10.853           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM #> 4:    6 1 191.5 10.877           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM #> 5:    6 1 192.0 10.866           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM #> 6:    6 1 192.5 11.105           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM visible <- read_nanodrop(path, min_wv = 400, max_wv = 700) range(visible$waves) #> [1] 400 700

code: read_nanodrop(   filepath,   min_wv = NULL,   max_wv = NULL,   remeasure_suffix = NULL,   error )

title: Read a NanoDrop One spectral export — read_nanodrop
text: filepath Path exported .tsv file. min_wv, max_wv Optional numeric wavelength bounds (inclusive). NULL (default) keeps full measured range. remeasure_suffix Optional suffix marks re-measurement, e.g. "e". set, sample named "" followed one named "Ae" treated replacement: "" measurements dropped "Ae" renamed "". Names ending suffix matching original (e.g. "Rinse" "Rins") left alone. NULL (default) disables . error Deprecated; use remeasure_suffix.

title: Read a NanoDrop One spectral export — read_nanodrop
text: data.table::data.table() columns: samps Sample name (character). waves Wavelength nm (numeric). abs Absorbance (numeric). measurement Position measurement block file (integer). timestamp Timestamp line written instrument (character).

title: Read a NanoDrop One spectral export — read_nanodrop
text: export consists one block per measurement: sample name line, timestamp line, Wavelength (nm) header line, optional // calibration lines, tab-separated wavelength/absorbance pairs. Blocks located header line, parser depend date format locale instrument. Every block becomes measurement, measuring sample name twice yields two measurements rather silently merging .

title: nanodRop 0.2.0
text: read_nanodrop() longer strips trailing “e” every sample name ending “e” (e.g. “Rinse” became “Rins”). read_nanodrop() longer merges measurements share sample name. read_nanodrop() longer returns NA sample names instrument writes timestamps format US 12-hour time. Blocks now found Wavelength (nm) header line. parse_waves() matches wavelengths tolerance (tol) instead exact floating point equality.

title: nanodRop 0.2.0
text: read_nanodrop() returns two new columns: measurement (block number file) timestamp. read_nanodrop(): min_wv max_wv take numbers default NULL (keep full range). Strings "190.0" still work. read_nanodrop(): re-measurement handling now opt-remeasure_suffix, renames sample original also present. changes default: set remeasure_suffix = "e" get old behaviour. error argument deprecated. New read_nanodrop_dir() reads every export folder. parse_waves() gains type = "ratio" (e.g. A260/A280), tol, id_cols. default now keeps repeated measurements separate. Absorbance columns come difference/ratio columns output. Removed magrittr, purrr, readr, rlang, stringr tidyr dependencies. Corrected documentation ds ds1.
